ogTitle: Chanthaburi 1-Day Itinerary — Riverside, Cathedral & Gem Market
ogDesc: Walk Chanthaburi old town in a single day: the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, the riverside cathedral, and the gem market — with timings and food spots locals actually go to.
intro: What makes Chanthaburi old town fun is how close everything sits together — you can cover most of the day on foot. Start at the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, a century-old neighborhood along the Chanthaburi River, then cross the bridge to pay your respects at the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, the largest Catholic church in Thailand, and finish at the Si Chan Road gem market, the biggest gem-trading spot in the country. This plan is built for real walking and real sightseeing across one full day.

blocks.html: If you only have one day in Chanthaburi, these three spots are the heart of the old town and well worth your time, because they all sit within walking distance of one another. The Chanthaboon Riverside Community and the cathedral are split only by the Chanthaburi River, with a bridge connecting the two banks, while the gem market is a short way off around Si Chan Road. You can reach everything on foot or with a quick ride. The one thing to plan around: the gem market is only open Friday to Sunday, so if you want to catch the buzz of traders working the street, come on a weekend.

items: Morning — walk the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, snack on old-school local food, and check out the heritage houses and street art
Late morning–noon — cross the bridge to the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception to see the gem-studded statue of Our Lady and the stained glass
Afternoon — walk the Si Chan Road gem market and watch the traders buying and selling for real
Evening — sit at a riverside cafe or finish with a plate of sen chan phat pu (crab-fried Chanthaburi noodles) before heading back

blocks.title: Pick the right day
blocks.html: Plan your trip for a Friday, Saturday or Sunday to hit all three spots, since the gem market only runs on those three days, roughly 10:00–15:00. The riverside community and the cathedral are open daily, but the shops in the community are busiest on weekends.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Chanthaburi trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Chanthaburi
items.note: Out and back in a day

items.activity: Start at the Chanthaboon Riverside Community on Sukhaphiban Road
items.note: Park near the temple grounds or along the road close to the community, then walk into the long lane that runs beside the river. There are still few people around in the morning, so it's easy to photograph the old wooden houses.

items.activity: Stop by the House No. 69 learning center and Boonyatthithi House
items.note: House No. 69 is a century-old home that displays the way of life in the community, while Boonyatthithi House is a building around 150 years old. Both are free to enter and easy to wander through.

items.activity: See the street art and the old Chinese medicine shop, Chang Guan An
items.note: An old Chinese pharmacy that still has its wooden herb drawers and the smell of dried herbs — a favorite photo corner. Along the way there are wall paintings telling stories of Chanthaburi at intervals.

items.activity: Try the old-school local food in the community
items.note: Rocket Brand Ice Cream is the community's legendary shop, with a childhood-nostalgia flavor. There's also Jay Iad noodles, kanom kai (egg sponge cakes), and soft rice crackers with a local dipping sauce — prices start in the low double digits (THB).

items.activity: Cross the suspension bridge to the cathedral side
items.note: The cathedral sits across the river from the riverside community, separated by the Chanthaburi River. It's only a few minutes' walk across the bridge, and the river views on both banks are lovely.

items.activity: See inside the cathedral, the gem-studded statue of Our Lady, and the stained glass
items.note: The largest Catholic church in Thailand, its highlights are the two pointed bell towers, the boat-hull ceiling, and the statue of Our Lady set with more than 200,000 gemstones. Open roughly Monday–Saturday 08:30–14:00.

items.activity: Stop for lunch around the old town
items.note: Sen chan phat pu (crab-fried Chanthaburi noodles) is the local signature, found at many shops around the old town, or you can head back for a seafood tom yum noodle soup in the riverside community.

blocks.title: Etiquette inside the cathedral
blocks.html: This is an active place of worship, so dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered, keep your voice down, and avoid visiting during Mass. If you're not sure of the times, check the cathedral's page before you go to be safe.

items.activity: Walk the Si Chan Road–Trok Krachang gem market
items.note: The biggest gem-trading spot in Thailand, open Friday–Sunday roughly 10:00–15:00. You'll see traders' tables lined up on both sides of the street, sorting stones with loupes — a sight that's hard to find anywhere else.

items.activity: Browse the gem shops and shop for gem-related souvenirs
items.note: If you're not set on buying a big stone, you can still walk around and take in the real trading scene. First-timers shouldn't rush to buy — gems come in many grades and prices, so ask around and compare several sellers first.

items.activity: Find a riverside cafe to wrap up the trip
items.note: Back around the riverside community there are several cafes, like C.A.P Cafe and People, decorated in an industrial style mixed with greenery. Sip a coffee by the river before heading home.

blocks.text: Food you shouldn't miss along the way

items.name: Sen chan phat pu (crab-fried noodles)
items.blurb: Chanthaburi's signature dish — chewy sen chan rice noodles stir-fried with fresh crab meat in a well-balanced sauce. Found at many shops around the old town, this is the one plate you have to try in Chanthaburi.

items.name: Rocket Brand Ice Cream
items.blurb: The legendary ice cream shop of the riverside community, with old-fashioned flavors that locals grew up on. Several flavors to cool you down while you walk.

items.name: Jay Iad noodles
items.blurb: A long-running noodle shop in the community, served generously with plenty of toppings — a light meal while you wander the riverside lane.

items.name: Seafood tom yum noodles
items.blurb: A coastal town means fresh seafood — a rich tom yum broth packed with seafood. Another dish people love to order in the old-town area.

items.name: Kanom kai and local sweets
items.blurb: Fragrant egg sponge cakes and old-recipe Thai sweets that have been sold in the community for decades. Good to take home as gifts.

items.name: Soft rice crackers with dipping sauce
items.blurb: A local Chanthaburi snack — soft dough sheets wrapped around a filling and topped with a punchy dipping sauce. Find it around the riverside community.

blocks.html: All three spots sit close together in the old-town area, so walking is the best way to get around. The lanes in the riverside community are narrow and one-way, which makes driving in awkward. The tip is to find parking near the temple grounds or along the roads on the edge of the community and walk in. Some places to stay in town also offer a shuttle to the community.

items: On foot — the riverside community and the cathedral connect across the bridge, and the gem market isn't far off
Private car — park on the outskirts of the community and walk in to avoid the narrow lanes
Motorbike taxi / hired ride — handy if you don't feel like walking back from the gem market to the riverside

blocks.title: Leave enough time
blocks.html: Taking it easy and unhurried, these three spots fill about half a day to most of a day, which leaves the evening free to move on somewhere else — like driving out to the sea at Laem Sing or Chao Lao Beach if you want to end the day with an ocean view.

faq.q: What can you do in Chanthaburi in one day?
faq.a: With just one day, the old town is the way to go since everything sits close together. Walk the Chanthaboon Riverside Community in the morning, cross the bridge to the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception late morning, then finish at the Si Chan Road gem market in the afternoon — you can comfortably cover it all on foot in a single day.

faq.q: What days and times is the Chanthaburi gem market open?
faq.a: The Si Chan Road gem market is open only on Friday, Saturday and Sunday, roughly 10:00–15:00. If you want to see the buzz of traders working the street, come on a weekend — weekdays are quiet.

faq.q: When can you visit the Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception?
faq.a: You can visit roughly Monday–Saturday 08:30–14:00. Sundays have limited hours because of Mass. Dress modestly with shoulders and knees covered, and check the times with the cathedral's page before you go to be safe.

faq.q: Can you walk between the Chanthaboon Riverside Community and the cathedral?
faq.a: Yes, easily. The two sit on opposite banks of the Chanthaburi River, connected by a bridge. Walking from the riverside community across the bridge to the cathedral takes just a few minutes.

faq.q: What's the best food in the Chanthaboon Riverside Community?
faq.a: The signatures are the legendary Rocket Brand Ice Cream, sen chan phat pu (crab-fried noodles), Jay Iad noodles, kanom kai (egg sponge cakes), and soft rice crackers with a local dipping sauce. Most prices run from tens to a bit over a hundred THB.
